result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent the diff changes the fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since that branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the predicate compares each calendar's externalId against a falsy value and can never match, so `calendarId` is always undefined there, whereas the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. This means legacy bookings (and references without externalCalendarId) get an undefined calendarId passed to `calendar.events.delete`, leaving events orphan

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback from the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Since that `find` predicate compares against a falsy `externalCalendarId` (undefined/null), it will never match a real calendar externalId, so the computed calendar id becomes undefined (or falls back to `primary` if later defaulted), which is not equivalent to the old behavior and can prevent deleting/updating events on non-primary calendars when references lack `externalCalendarId`.
